key_insight: Linking real field flips to real ACT/REF histories is the one dataset that could show hammer and retention margins are over-designed.
killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die SEC hides single-bit flips. 3,200 DIMMs give ~30-150 CE DIMMs/yr, mostly permanent faults, so few hammer events. A 1 s ring needs ~1-2 GB/s per subchannel.
decisive_experiment: Before building hardware, mine existing MCA/ECS CE logs from one partner fleet (10k+ servers) for row-adjacent clustering. If <1% of CEs look hammer-like, stop.
prior_art: DDR5 protocol analyzers (Teledyne LeCroy/FuturePlus); ETH SAFARI DRAM Bender lab characterization; Meta fleet study (Meza, DSN 2015).

key_insight: Retiring subarrays through host/CXL page tables instead of fuses recovers dies that fail only on redundancy. The bigger prize is HBM stack harvesting (selling 11-of-12-die stacks).
killer_doubt: Fallout is mostly global shorts, IDD and periphery fails, not mat-local. At ~85% yield that recovers ~3-6% more bits, not 10-20%. Dead mats also leak.
decisive_experiment: With one vendor or OSAT, sort fail-bit maps of 10k rejected dies into mat-local vs global, then demo an FPGA CXL controller retiring a die's bad subarray rows. ~$200k.
prior_art: Half-good DRAM (ZX Spectrum 4532 parts, 'audio RAM'); GPU die harvesting; DDR5 PPR/sPPR; Linux page offlining.

key_insight: Real sense amps plus real BEOL oxide arrays for ~$50-150k: the decisive testbed for charge-transfer sensing (N-04), ECC-margin tails (N-62) and multi-level drift maps.
killer_doubt: Die-level litho and planarization on ~10 mm2 diced die. Sky130 top-metal pitch is ~3 um and Al BEOL tops out near 400 C: IGZO anneal <=350 C.
decisive_experiment: One GF180/Sky130 shuttle with 64 sense amps plus pad openings; post-process a 4 kb IGZO 1T1C/2T0C array at <=350 C; measure signal vs Cs and the 85 C retention tail.
prior_art: Shulaker et al. (Nature 2017): CNFET+RRAM on foundry CMOS; Weebit ReRAM in SkyWater 130 nm; imec IGZO 2T0C. Not as a shared open testbed.

key_insight: Bistability bought with pump power instead of capacitor size: a state-dependent varactor plus a rectifying diode. Holding 13 pA needs only ~130 Hz at 0.1 fC/cycle.
killer_doubt: Separatrix is set by diode Vf and varactor flatband. BEOL sigma is ~50-100 mV against a ~200 mV window, so it fails at 6 sigma over 3e10 cells.
decisive_experiment: Bench a discrete varactor+diode cell, then build 1,000 IGZO MOS-varactor/Schottky pairs in a university fab. Map the zero crossings of Ipump(V)-Ileak(V), the window, and its sigma at 85 C. <$300k.
prior_art: Goto parametron (1954); TI RTD-based tunneling SRAM (van der Wagt/Seabaugh, late 1990s); triage N-07 tunnel-diode latch.

key_insight: Every new cell lacks published retention, disturb and soft-error failure-rate data. A shared JEDEC-style qualification lab is genuinely useful infrastructure.
killer_doubt: The premise is half wrong: Z-RAM and T-RAM stalled on margin and variability at scale. Patents filed 2003-2010 expire by ~2030. A real qualification line costs >$50M.
decisive_experiment: Audit the named estates for expiry, live claims and documented failure modes. If <30% of claims survive past 2030, drop the pool and fund only an open reliability-test lab.
prior_art: CHIPS Act NSTC/NAPMP prototyping programs; SEMATECH-style consortia; JEDEC qualification flows.

key_insight: Regeneration replaces correction: KV and activations can be re-derived, so a detect-only CRC is enough. Dense decode already activates every KV row each step, which refreshes it by access.
killer_doubt: At 4x relaxation, unprofiled raw BER ~1e-6 gives ~8e-3 errors per 1 KB block. A 40 GB cache (4e7 blocks) then needs ~3e5 weight-bound recomputes/s.
decisive_experiment: Inject DRAM-Bender-measured retention error maps (0.25-2 s, 45-85 C, including VRT) into vLLM KV blocks with CRC+recompute. Measure the tokens/s lost against the refresh energy saved. Software only.
prior_art: Flikker (ASPLOS 2011) relaxed refresh for non-critical data; EDEN (MICRO 2019) approximate DRAM for DNNs; vLLM recompute-on-preemption; Smart Refresh.

key_insight: Low-thermal-budget memories drift (IGZO PBTI Vt), so references and refresh learned in the field will be necessary, as NAND read-retry proved.
killer_doubt: The mechanism is already standard (SSD FTL read-retry, updatable CXL controller firmware, DDR5 ECS/PRAC). The subscription is pricing, not a physics or supply gain, and ns-latency rules out FTL-style retries.
decisive_experiment: Not needed as a standalone invention. Fold adaptive-reference firmware into the I-01312 controller prototype and measure drift-tracking gain on IGZO test arrays.
prior_art: NAND SSD FTLs with read-retry and LDPC soft decode; RAIDR/AVATAR adaptive refresh; field-updatable CXL memory controllers.

key_insight: Rank refresh is set by the weakest die. Matching dies by measured retention lets the controller set tREFI per rank.
killer_doubt: VRT cells hop retention states after test, so one-time profiling misses them and 2-4x longer tREFI needs ECC anyway. Temperature-scaled refresh already harvests most margin below 85 C.
decisive_experiment: Profile 200 DDR5 dies at 64/128/256 ms and 45/85 C each month for 6 months on DRAM Bender. Count new failures per bin after binning. <$300k.
prior_art: RAIDR (ISCA 2012); Liu et al. ISCA 2013 retention/VRT study; REAPER (ISCA 2017); AVATAR; DDR5 temperature-based refresh scaling.

key_insight: Speculative decoding's rejection sampling stays exact for whatever draft distribution was actually computed, so draft-side memory errors cost only acceptance rate.
killer_doubt: Draft models are 1-8B parameters (2-16 GB) per accelerator and want HBM bandwidth. That absorbs <<1% of DRAM output, so the impact on the weak-bin market is negligible.
decisive_experiment: Inject bit flips at BER 1e-6 to 1e-4 into a draft model's weights and KV in vLLM, and measure the acceptance-rate loss. About a week of GPU time.
prior_art: EDEN (MICRO 2019) approximate DRAM for DNNs; speculative decoding (Leviathan 2023; Chen 2023). Weak-bin draft hosting: none found.

key_insight: Page-level codes turn the retention tail into a parity budget. At raw BER 1e-4, a 4 KB BCH needs ~1.5% parity (t~30), buying 4-16x refresh relaxation with no new fab.
killer_doubt: DDR5 runs in-DRAM TRR inside REF commands, so 8x fewer REFs means 8x fewer hammer-mitigation slots at HC~1k; RFM/PRAC is needed. Self-refresh cannot be stretched.
decisive_experiment: Build an FPGA CXL/DDR5 controller with 4 KB BCH/LDPC. Run commodity and retention-reject DIMMs at 0.25-2 s refresh, 45-85 C, with RFM on. Log raw BER, VRT and hammer flips for 3 months. ~$500k.
prior_art: Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010): strong BCH cut eDRAM refresh 93% (via search snippet); Morphable ECC (DSN 2015); patent US10691532; triage N-62/N-63.

key_insight: Works as a one-chip-per-codeword onramp: put at most one unproven second-source chip (e.g. from a U.S. entrant) in each chipkill codeword, so its systematic flaws are always correctable.
killer_doubt: As written it fails. Every chip sees the same ACT, so a vendor-systematic flaw hits 3-5 chips of a 10-chip DDR5 x4 codeword. Chipkill corrects one.
decisive_experiment: Build 20 RDIMMs with 9 incumbent chips plus 1 'risky' chip per subchannel. Run TRRespass-style hammer and 2 s retention stress, and show zero UEs against single-vendor controls. ~$200k.
prior_art: Chipkill/SDDC (IBM, AMD); vendor/lot mixing in RAID disk arrays. Vendor-mixed DIMM codewords: none found.

key_insight: Unlimited magnetic endurance in a transistorless vertical string; ALD soft-magnetic tubes in DRAM-like holes are a credible process idea.
killer_doubt: The read collapses. A 5x50 nm tube bit holds ~2.5e-16 Wb: a 1 ns rotation gives ~0.2 uV against ~100 uV noise. AMR is even in M: state-blind.
decisive_experiment: Run micromagnetic plus circuit simulation of a 50 nm NiFe tube bit, then fabricate one 200 nm ALD tube with a radial GMR spin-valve and show >=5% state-dependent dR. ~$300k.
prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, 1960s-70s spacecraft); Parkin racetrack; cylindrical nanotube domain-wall memories; triage N-82 capacitor-hole racetrack.
